question: Along the restricted weak-cover family E_alpha: y^2 = x(x - alpha)(x - sigma alpha) over F_{p^6} (alpha in F_{p^6} \ F_{p^2}, #E = 4l, l prime), how does the cold complete cost of the frozen quadratic-remainder graph index calculus grow with l, compared with the cheapest registered Pollard rho on the same fresh public targets, over six growing sizes p = 127, 223, 383, 661, 1153, 2017 (b = log2 l from about 39.9 to 63.9)? Report per-size ratios as the distance remaining and fitted exponents with intervals; no tier claim is licensed by this draft.

claims.text: Per size, the ratio sum C_IC / sum C_rho_ref over the n admitted fresh public targets, with its 95% paired bootstrap interval, on metric M2 (complete-process CPU seconds) and, only if gate G-cov passes, on M1 (complete counted GAE at the section 5a band).

claims.if_not_supported: An interval containing 1 is reported as unresolved at that size; no ranking is written.

claims.text: The fitted exponent alpha_IC of ln C_IC against ln l (and against ln p^6), with its 95% stratified bootstrap interval, and the paired difference alpha_IC - alpha_rho_ref.
claims.if_supported: An exponent estimate on the declared path; T2 still requires the held-out size and complete counts that this draft cannot provide (see distance_remaining).
claims.if_not_supported: An interval for alpha_IC - alpha_rho containing 0 is reported as no exponent difference resolved on this path.

claims.text: Descent residual counts R per run follow a negative-binomial draw with 2 required successes; the pooled acceptance rate pi_hat = sum(A) / sum(R) per size and the descent-normalised expected IC cost E[C_IC] = mean(C_nd) + (2 / pi_hat) * mean(c_res).
claims.if_supported: A model-based secondary reading that separates acceptance rate from per-residual cost; never substituted for the measured C1/C2 numbers.
claims.if_not_supported: If accepted descents per run are not 2, or pi_hat differs across sizes by more than its interval, the normalisation is withdrawn and only measured costs are reported.

claims.if_supported: The fit can see a known exponent and does not invent a difference between two arms of equal exponent.
claims.if_not_supported: The fit or instrument is invalid; C2 is not reported.

hypotheses.statement: The graph IC's cold cost grows with a smaller exponent in l than rho's 1/2 on this family, because its collection and linear algebra scale with the factor base (about p, so l^{1/6} per element) while its descent costs a near-constant number of F_p operations per residual; at the small sizes the descent's fixed cost flattens the measured slope.
hypotheses.mechanism: Joux-Vitse cover-and-decomposition over F_{p^6}: genus-3 cover over F_{p^2}, factor base indexed by F_p (about p/2 classes), Nagao decomposition of 6 points with an F_p-rational sextic, one success in about 720 attempts heuristically; observed 2 accepted in 1506, 1728 and 3415 residuals at p1009 [pcc:unverified].

predictions.minimum_effect: alpha_IC - alpha_rho_ref < 0 with the Holm-adjusted one-sided 95% interval wholly below 0; the local slope of the IC between the two largest sizes is reported beside the global fit.

data_seen.measured: p1009 fixed known-answer instance: IC median 20.71 s, rho plain b16 median 111.40 s
p1009 one fixture: IC 15.1-31.5 s, rho 36.9-119.8 s per config

provenance.decisive_scope: fresh public targets at six sizes; no size other than p1009 has any recorded IC run on this pipeline

predictions.minimum_effect: At p127 and p223 the IC ratio to rho_ref exceeds 1 (rho costs under a second there; IC's descent alone is several seconds). Stated so that a fixed-cost-dominated small-size regime is expected, not a failure.

family.rule: jv_cover.rs weak family over F_{q^3}, q = p^2: alpha uniform in F_{p^6} \ F_{p^2} from the target stream; accept when Cover admits alpha (N, F in F_q[x]), j(E) is in neither F_{p^2} nor F_{p^3}, #E = 4l with l prime < 2^64 (BSGS in the library's Hasse window, two extra points killed), and no embedding degree k <= 1000; then the frozen pipeline's own public validation (spec_from_curve: transfer of G and Q to Jac_H non-degenerate) in the admission pass.
family.path: p doubles about every 1.74x: p in {127, 223, 383, 661, 1153, 2017}; m = 6 fixed (n = 3 over F_{p^2}); cofactor h = 4 fixed; genus-3 cover fixed; factor base = F_p (about p points); Nagao ng = 6; method parameters exactly as the nagao-e2e frozen baseline (full factor base, 1024-B collection batches, full p^2 B cap, 65536 source cap, 8192 descent residual cap, 32 accepted cap, degree 24, staircase 64).
family.bounds_tier: medium (field bits 41.9 to 65.9, all within 32 < bits <= 96)
family.size_bands: B1 (32 <= b < 64) at every size; p2017 sits at b = 63.87, just inside B1.
family.density_disclosure: Dry run (nonce DRYRUN-NOT-A-BEACON-20261118, 3 targets per size): admissible alpha per attempt 3/46, 3/113, 3/146, 3/221, 3/277, 3/125 for p = 127 ... 2017; all rejections were #E not 4 * prime. Descriptive only.
family.weakness_disclosure: Weak by construction: GHS/cover-weak (genus-3 cover over F_{p^2}); the family is a known weak subfamily (SUCCESS_CRITERIA section 5 item 5) and results are for this subfamily only. Not anomalous (l != p). Embedding degree > 1000 checked per target. j outside proper subfields, so the only automorphism is negation (gamma = 2) and no Frobenius fold applies to rho.
family.upper_limit: l must stay below 2^64 for the frozen library (u64 scalars); p <= 2039. This blocks the T2 held-out size (8 bits above the largest fitted size).

Both the round and C are recorded; anyone recomputes the nonce. Neither the protocol author nor the runner can predict X when C is made.

nonce_scheme.admission_and_replacement: Indices 0, 1, 2, ... per size in increasing order; a target is admitted when the generator accepts it and the frozen worker's public validation (no solve, no answer) accepts its transfer. The measured set is the first n admitted indices. Every refused index is listed with its reason. No other exclusion.

sample_size.justification: SUCCESS_CRITERIA T1 item 1 requires at least 32 targets below b = 64. Noise model: rho cost per run is Rayleigh-like (CV about 0.52); IC cost CV is f_d * sqrt((1 - pi)/2) ~ 0.707 f_d from the negative-binomial descent (f_d = descent share, about 0.37 at p1009 and near 1 at p127), plus a small collection term. With n = 32, the per-size ratio interval half-width is about 1.96 * sqrt(CV_ic^2 + CV_rho^2) / sqrt(32): about +-30% at p127 and +-20% at p2017 (log scale). The exponent SE from 6 sizes is about 0.12 / (5.7 * sqrt(6)) ~ 0.009, so statistical width is small next to model misfit (fixed descent cost, polylog factors); curvature is therefore reported, not hidden.
sample_size.descent_f4_accounting: Critic F4: with 2 successes per run, the pooled pi_hat per size rests on 2n = 64 successes (relative SE about 12.5%), the same information as averaging measured costs. Descent normalisation therefore separates rate from per-residual cost but does not shrink the variance; only more successes do (more targets, or the optional descent-probe arm). Any IC-versus-IC comparison is paired on the worker seed so both arms consume the identical residual stream (checked by stream signature), which removes the NB term; where a candidate changes the stream, require at least 100 pooled successes per arm per size (n = 50 targets, or the probe) before reading a descent difference.

timeout_seconds.rho_per_run: step cap 20x sqrt(pi l / 2) (probability of reaching it is negligible); hitting it is a recorded failure charged at consumed cost

stopping_rules.rule: Fixed n = 32 admitted public targets per size; no sequential adding after looking at an interval (adding targets starts a new attempt).

Sizes run in ascending order; each size completes before the next starts. Global budget 80 CPU-hours; if the remaining projected cost of the next size exceeds the budget, stop before it and report the completed sizes (at least 4 needed for C2).
If more than 2 of 32 IC runs at a size fail or hit the cap, report the success probability and stop the larger sizes.
Positive controls (planted, bridge) run first per size and per host; any miss stops that size and the instrument is invalid.

invalidation_rules: A row from a binary, generator or nonce other than the frozen ones is inadmissible.
A recovered scalar not replayed as [k]G = Q on E is a failure, not a solve.
An IC run whose worker reads anything but public curve, G, Q, l is invalid (the generator emits no answer field; the checker refuses answer-like keys).
A preempted row's clock is invalid; the restarted row is used and the attempt is listed.

decision_rule.text: Per size: R_s = sum C_IC / sum C_rho_ref over the n admitted targets; rho_ref is the registered rho configuration with the smallest sum at that size (per weight for M1). Report R_s with its 95% paired bootstrap interval as the distance remaining; 'below rho at size p on M2' only if the Holm-adjusted interval lies wholly below 1, 'above' only if wholly above, else 'unresolved'. Exponent: OLS of ln(mean C) on ln(mean l) over sizes for ic-graph, rho_ref, each rho configuration and each IC phase, also on ln p^6; 95% stratified bootstrap (targets resampled within size, 2000 resamples). Read alpha_IC - alpha_rho_ref only if C4's controls pass; report local slopes between consecutive sizes and a quadratic-in-ln-l fit beside the line. Descent-normalised costs are a labelled secondary reading.
decision_rule.multiple_comparisons: Holm over the 6 per-size ratio tests plus the slope test, per metric (family-wise 0.05); every attempt in the family is listed.
